extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, economists, and empirical researchers studying patent litigation; patent litigators and policy analysts interested in cross-technology litigation outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Regression-specification and variable list used to analyze patent litigation outcomes across technologies, districts, and industries; includes outcome definitions, covariates, significance notation, and model-fit statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table significance & layout notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Top row = Coefficient; * = p<.10, ** = p<.05, *** = p<.01; Bottom row = Std. error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used across appendices to interpret reported regression coefficients and their statistical significance; appears repeatedly as explanatory note for each table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model fit and test statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported model-fit and test statistics include N, r2_p, ll, chi2, p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each appendix/table reports sample size (N), pseudo-R^2 (r2_p), log-likelihood (ll), chi-squared statistic (chi2), and p-value to assess overall model fit and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison Dummy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison Dummy = Chemistry (or Consumer Goods & Services Uses depending on table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemistry (or specified category) is used as the base/reference category for technology/industry comparisons in regressions; coefficients for other dummies are relative to this comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Origin of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Origin of Patent (variable included as covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary/indicator capturing whether the patent originated outside the U.S.; included to test whether origin predicts litigation outcomes or invalidity findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted Number of Citations Received
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjusted Number of Citations Received (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A measure of patent citations adjusted as described in the paper; used to proxy patent value or technological importance in regressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Prior Art References
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Prior Art References (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of prior art references associated with the patent; included to assess relationship between prior art quantity and invalidity/outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Claims (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw count of claims in the patent; used to control for claim scope/complexity when analyzing litigation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of Patent at Current Litigation Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Age of Patent at Current Litigation Filing (T) (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time (age) of the patent when the litigation was filed; included to control for lifecycle effects on validity or outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Defendants
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Defendants (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count of defendants in the suit; used to examine whether multi-defendant suits correlate with different outcomes or motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Asserted Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Asserted Patents (W) (covariate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count of patents asserted in the litigation; controls for case complexity or plaintiff strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology category dummies (mechanical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical (Primary + Secondary) technology dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for cases/patents classified as mechanical (primary or secondary); coefficients measure difference versus comparison dummy (chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology category dummies (electronics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronics (Primary + Secondary) technology dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for electronics technology; used to compare litigation outcomes across technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology category dummies (biotech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biotech (Primary + Secondary) technology dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for biotechnology patents; used to show biotech-specific effects on litigation outcomes (noting biotech owners fare poorly in reported results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology category dummies (optics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optics (Primary + Secondary) technology dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for optics technology; included for cross-technology comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology category dummies (software)
rubrics_metrics.description: Software (Primary + Secondary) technology dummy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for software patents; paper notes software owners fare poorly—this dummy captures that effect; also subdivided into software BM and software NBM in some specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software BM / Software NBM subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Software BM (subset of Primary) and Software NBM (subset of Primary) dummies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-classifications of software patents used in restricted specifications to separate business-method-like patents (BM) from non-BM software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Definitive Winner
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner Definitive Winner (outcome variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary outcome indicating whether the patent owner was the ultimate winner in the litigation (definitive outcome). Used as dependent variable in some regressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SJ Invalidity - All
rubrics_metrics.description: SJ Invalidity-All (summary-judgment invalidity at any stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether an invalidity finding was reached at summary judgment; used as outcome to study invalidity incidence across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: SJ Noninfringement plus Stipulated Judgment of Noninfringement
rubrics_metrics.description: SJ Noninfringement Plus Stip. Jgmt of Noninfringement (summary-judgment or stipulated noninfringement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures cases resolved at summary judgment or by stipulation on noninfringement; used to analyze noninfringement resolution patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner - Trial Winner
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner-Trial Winner (outcome variable for trial-stage wins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether patent owner prevailed at trial; distinguished from definitive winner depending on later events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity - All (any stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity-All--Any stage (indicator that invalidity was found at any litigation stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate invalidity indicator capturing invalidity findings at any procedural stage (SJ, trial, post-trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity - 102 Prior Art (any stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity-102 Prior Art-All--Any stage (anticipation/prior art invalidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for invalidity findings based on 35 U.S.C. §102-type prior art at any stage of litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity - 103 Obviousness (any stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity-103-Obviousness--Any Stage (obviousness invalidity indicator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for invalidity based on obviousness (§103) at any stage; separate from 102 and 112 invalidity types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity - 112 Indefiniteness (any stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity-112-Indefiniteness--Any Stage (indefiniteness-based invalidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures invalidity findings under 35 U.S.C. §112 for indefiniteness at any litigation stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity - 112 Inadequate Disclosure (any stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity-112-Inadequate Disclosure--Any stage (written-description/enablement deficiencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator for invalidity due to inadequate disclosure (written description/enablement) under §112 at any stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Infringement (Literal + DOE) - Any stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Infringement (Literal + Doctrine of Equivalents) - Any stage (infringement indicator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome/covariate capturing direct infringement findings either literal or under DOE at any stage of litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: District indicator dummies
rubrics_metrics.description: District dummies include TX ED, DE D, CA ND, CA CD, CA SD, NY SD, IL ND, WI WD, NJ D, MA D, VA ED, OH ND, TX SD, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District fixed-effects included to capture forum effects; table notes 'All Other Districts (multi-collinearity too high)' where collinearity issues arise; district coefficients show local forum effects on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry category dummies
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry dummies reported: Computer & Other Electronics, Semiconductor, Pharmaceutical, Medical Devices/Methods/Other Medical, Biotech (industry), Communication, Transportation-Including Automotive, Construction, Energy, Goods & Services for Industrial & Business Uses, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry-level indicators used in regressions to detect industry-specific litigation patterns; some tables use Consumer Goods & Services as comparison category.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Other Districts / Multicollinearity note
rubrics_metrics.description: All Other Districts (multi-collinearity too high) used in some specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including many district dummies, some are grouped due to multicollinearity; authors flag this as a limitation of district-fixed-effects specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of selection effects in interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection mechanisms may differ across technology areas and may bias litigated-patent samples; litigated patents may be valid when issued but invalid when adjudicated (e.g., Myriad patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors caution that litigation is complex and selection effects could explain observed cross-technology differences; readers should consider these caveats when generalizing results.
